solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Panda, one of four in trauma

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a scar is the lasting mark of a trauma
a quad is one of four born together, a quadruplet

explanation.surface: A panda bear somehow ends up as one of quadruplets in a medical emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panda' is not the bear: a panda car was the British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in blue and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda car is old British slang for a police patrol vehicle, which is the same thing as this.

clue.text: Speaking character's line

indicators.note: speaking says the letter is spoken out loud, so we go by how it sounds

parts.note: the character here is the letter Q, a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor delivers a character's line of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a role in a play, but it is a printed letter; said out loud, Q sounds like a word for a line of people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn is the same as this, especially in British usage.

clue.text: Number Ten is a cheat, untrustworthy

indicators.note: untrustworthy letters cannot be relied on to stay in order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Downing Street, Number Ten, stands accused of cheating and being untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as in Number Ten, the Prime Minister's residence, but it means something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A number here is a thing that makes numb, which is exactly what a drug blocking sensation does.

clue.text: Tired oarsman capsizing in vessel

indicators.note: in tells us the turned word goes inside the container

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel

indicators.note: capsizing turns a boat over, so in a down light the word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: An exhausted rower tips over while still in his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' fits the oarsman's surface but only flips his word in this down light; 'vessel' suggests a boat yet is merely a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn down by worry and fatigue looks tired, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Why the abandonment? Unscheduled dip? Apparently so!

definitions.text: Why the abandonment? Unscheduled dip? Apparently so!

parts.words: Why the abandonment? Unscheduled dip? Apparently so!
parts.note: read as a cricket scoreboard announcement: the reason a match was abandoned, the wet weather having given everyone an unplanned soaking

explanation.surface: Someone asks why an event was called off, wondering if an unexpected swim was to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a common British summer sport, matches are halted when it rains; the 'dip' is the unwanted soaking the weather gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather halting a cricket match is the standard reason given for a game being abandoned.

clue.text: White scoffing at taste

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the first word swallows the second

parts.note: white means pale

explanation.surface: A white person laughs at someone's taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' looks like mocking, but here it is British slang for eating greedily, so PALE takes in AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Your palate is your sense of taste, as in a refined palate for wine.

clue.text: Fruit, tripe and a vegetable, cut

parts.note: tripe is worthless nonsense, also called pap

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its end letter

parts.note: a yam is a starchy root vegetable

explanation.surface: A shopping list of fruit, tripe and a chopped vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims YAM to YA.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical fruit is also called pawpaw, an orange-fleshed melon-like fruit.

clue.text: Garland from Algeria, regularly seen

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: A flower garland brought from Algeria is often seen.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hawaiian word names a flower wreath worn around the neck, a garland.

clue.text: Thin implement designed incorrectly? First of pieces lodged

indicators.note: lodged means stuck inside, so the letter goes into the phrase

parts.note: a thin implement designed wrongly would be too thick, the phrase read as two words

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A poorly made slender tool has bits of something stuck in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey step: a thin tool made badly would be TOO THICK. 'lodged' puts P from 'pieces' inside it, and pieces lodged in teeth are what this tool removes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin pointed stick used for cleaning between the teeth, a slender implement.

clue.text: Strain put on salesman, having to retire

indicators.note: put on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a strain is a tune or melody, an air

explanation.surface: A salesman under too much pressure has to give up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' means go somewhere, as in 'repair to the bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off to a place, as in withdrawing to another room, is an old sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Little terror with no teacher sent back to jail

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a little terror

indicators.note: sent back means these words are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A naughty child with no teacher is sent back to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns NO SIR into RISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone up is to jail them, both verbs of confinement.

clue.text: Information far from the old north?

parts.note: something far from old is new
the compass point furthest from north is south, S

explanation.surface: A quizzical remark that information comes from somewhere remote from the old north.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: 'far from' does duty for both pieces, giving the opposite of old and the opposite of north.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events are information, the ordinary meaning of this word.

clue.text: Weak character seen in panto

definitions.meaning: Widow Twankey's son in the pantomime Aladdin, a British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: A feeble role in a pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale, watery and indecisive things are called weak in this colloquial reduplicated adjective.

clue.text: I avoid usual excitement, in a couple of senses

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone avoids the usual thrills, in a couple of ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Using both sound and sight engages two of the senses, hearing and vision.

clue.text: Casanova reluctant to reach a port

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A famous lover is unwilling to travel to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova is the archetypal seducer, and this name from an old play means the same type of man.

clue.text: Wine lover's pigeonhole no good, needing sorting

indicators.note: needing sorting says the remaining letters are put in a fresh order
no here means without, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A wine enthusiast's filing system is a mess and needs tidying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' takes G out of PIGEONHOLE, leaving PIEONHOLE for 'needing sorting' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek-derived word means a connoisseur of wine, someone devoted to it.

clue.text: Girl in chains almost finding platform

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: Daisy is a girl's name, and also the flower in daisy chains

explanation.surface: A girl in shackles finds a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chains' is not about captivity: daisy chains are flowers strung together, so the girl is Daisy, and 'almost' drops her final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform at one end of a hall for speakers is called this.

clue.text: Great number in stock, a collection of vessels

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to stock a shelf is to fill it
a lot is a great number

explanation.surface: A large number of boats held in reserve form a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like a noun but is the verb 'fill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet of ships or boats is a group of vessels.

clue.text: Reef bird?

definitions.meaning: a reef is a type of square tie in rope, used in sailing
a small wading shore bird of the sandpiper family

explanation.definitionFit: A reef is one kind of rope tie, and a small sandpiper shares this name.

clue.text: Fools, with hair on cheek swept over

indicators.note: on means placed after, the hair following the cheek
swept over means turned the other way round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impudence
locks are hair

explanation.surface: Idiots with hair combed across their faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swept over' turns LIP into PIL. PILLOCK is British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for idiots, a mild insult much like nitwits.

clue.text: Examine essay, not right, but brief

parts.note: to scan is to examine

indicators.note: not says a letter is taken away

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Read through an essay that isn't correct, but keep it short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' means an attempt, not a written piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely enough, meagre or skimpy, as in a brief outfit.

clue.text: Card captures another card (clubs), taking first of tricks — but is he out of it?

indicators.note: captures means one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a spade is a playing card of that suit
an ace is a playing card
C is the bridge abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A card game where one card takes another and a trick, but one player seems vague.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a game of bridge, but 'captures' is the container signal; 'taking' just joins on the opening letter of 'tricks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy, absent-minded person is often called this, as if not on the same planet.

clue.text: Among seraphim, pious Bantu warriors

indicators.note: among says the answer is found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Zulu fighters mingling with devout angels.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment of Zulu or other Bantu soldiers is called this.

clue.text: Bird lacking lithium, finding nut

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a pelican is a large water bird
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A bird short of a metal finds something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes LI from PELICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a smooth-shelled nut from a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Untouched instrument

definitions.meaning: a small early keyboard instrument like a harpsichord

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pure or untouched, and the noun names an early keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Yank set up to form corporation

indicators.note: set up in a down light means read upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to yank is to tug

explanation.surface: An American founds a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American and 'corporation' like a company; it is a jokey word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is old humorous slang for a paunch, the belly.

clue.text: Found article in food

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lunch is a meal, food
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Discovered an item in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a business is to start it up, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Privileged few first to gain access

indicators.note: first to means take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: entry means access

explanation.surface: The elite are the first allowed in.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-born upper classes form a small privileged group.

clue.text: Young horse (a grey) whipped, nothing held back

indicators.note: held means the shuffled letters hold the other piece inside
whipped means beaten about, so the letters are mixed up
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A grey colt is beaten, with nothing held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' scrambles 'a grey' into YEARG, and 'held back' does two jobs in sequence: 'back' reverses nothing, 'held' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse in its second year, between one and two years old, is called this.
